C.title: D. Reading comprehension
intro: A company introduced a four-day working week as a six-month experiment. Employees kept their existing salaries, but teams had to redesign meetings and agree on service cover. The aim was to reduce unnecessary work rather than compress five unchanged days into four.

At the end of the trial, staff reported lower stress and fewer interruptions. Sales remained stable, although customer waiting times increased during two unusually busy weeks. The managers acknowledged that the trial coincided with a quieter season, so stable sales alone could not prove that the new schedule was more productive.

Instead of announcing a permanent change immediately, the company extended the trial into its busiest quarter. It also collected customer feedback and compared results with a similar team that had kept the old schedule. The managers hoped that these additional comparisons would help distinguish the effects of the schedule from other influences.

questions.question: What was the experiment intended to reduce?
Why did the managers treat the sales figures cautiously?
options: The trial took place in a quieter season

questions.question: Which problem occurred during two busy weeks?
Why compare results with a team on the old schedule?
options: To remove the need for customer feedback
To help separate the schedule’s effects from other factors
To prove all teams are identical

questions.question: Which description best fits the managers’ approach?
options: Certain that the experiment had failed

E.title: E. Paragraph writing
intro: Write a connected paragraph evaluating a change at work or in education. Explain its intended benefit, one possible disadvantage, what evidence you would collect, and the conditions under which you would recommend it. Use a clear position and supporting reasons. Aim for 120–160 words.
